meaning: Answer map for Q-MORAL-GROUNDING (what makes something objectively good or evil?). O'Connor's emotivism: no objective grounding, because moral statements have no truth value (OCONNOR-DESTINY-ETHICS-EMOTIVISM; in 2016, no objective moral truths, OCONNOR-TUREK-EVIL-NO-OBJECTIVE-MORAL-TRUTHS). Catholic theory: goodness is the same in reality as being in act (ST I q.5 a.1); evil is the privation of a due good (q.48 a.3); 'there is evil' is true when such a privation is in a subject (q.48 a.2 ad 2). Naturalist moral realism: unexplained for now, since no proponent text can be pinned (candidate NATURALIST-MORAL-REALISM-RAILTON). This result is the Catholic coverage cell for the evidence item 'there is evil' (the general premise of ST I q.2 a.3 obj. 1): under the shared background the Catholic theory entails it. The theory enters as one bundle hypothesis (`Catholic s`), and bind-check binds each of its 14 conjuncts to a premise listed here. The emotivism cell (contradicted) is POE-EXTERNAL-PREMISE-VS-EMOTIVISM, but that cell concerns the narrower moral-evil premise (man-made evil). Aquinas' malum is privation, metaphysical as well as moral, so the two cells are distinct evidence items and are not merged. The Catholic cell for moral evil specifically (culpa, ST I q.48 a.5) is not formalized yet. Proof shape: two steps (deficiency plus privation gives evil in some being; propositional truth gives the premise). Most listed commitments are unused, because the cell is stated for the whole theory.
